1.title: Claude Code Operation
1.text: Welcome to Module fifteen: Claude Code Operation. This module covers the skills claude code operation. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. The core components: Rules, Skills, Commands, Agents and Agent Memory. Features: session management, slash commands, headless, streaming and auto mode. The Claude dot M D hierarchy, repository initialization and settings.json.

1.title: Case Check-In: Tidewater Rolls Out Claude Code
1.text: Our running case is Tidewater Insurance. Tidewater Rolls Out Claude Code. Fifty engineers will use Claude Code on the claims platform. The lead wants shared standards, reusable workflows, specialist helpers, and safe automation.

1.title: Core Components
1.text: Core Components. The figure shows this: Claude Code components: instructions (Claude dot M D, rules), workflows (skills, commands), specialists (agents) and configuration (settings.json).

1.title: Core Components, continued
1.text: Core Components, continued. Claude dot M D. What it is: Persistent instructions loaded at session start. Where it lives: User home dot Claude, Claude dot M D, project Claude dot M D or the dot Claude Claude dot M D file (shared), subdirectories. Rules. What it is: Topic files, optionally scoped to paths with a glob. Where it lives: the markdown files in the dot Claude rules folder. Skills. What it is: On-demand procedures (Skill dot M D with frontmatter). Where it lives: the dot Claude skills folder less than name greater than or or home dot Claude skills. Commands. What it is: or name shortcuts; custom commands are markdown files. Where it lives: the dot Claude commands folder (shared) or home dot Claude commands (personal); now merged into skills. Agents. What it is: Subagents defined as markdown with frontmatter: own context, tools and optional memory. Where it lives: the dot Claude agents folder or about or the dot Claude agents folder.

1.title: Core Components, continued
1.text: Core Components, continued. Agent memory. What it is: Knowledge a subagent keeps across sessions (user, project or local scope); also auto memory: notes Claude writes itself from your corrections. Where it lives: Memory directories managed by Claude Code. settings.json. What it is: Permissions, hooks, environment, plugins, model. Where it lives: User, shared project, project local, managed.

1.title: The CLAUDE.md hierarchy
1.text: The Claude dot M D hierarchy. User level: personal, not shared. Project level: shared through version control. Directory level: applies to work in that folder. Files are combined, not overridden; keep them short and specific. slash init analyzes the repository and creates a starting Claude dot M D (build and test commands, conventions); review and edit it. slash memory shows which memory files are loaded. Repository initialization checklist: run slash init, commit the project Claude dot M D, add shared dot Claude settings.json (permissions, hooks), add rules, skills and commands the team needs, and keep personal overrides in local files. Exam tip: Team standards belong in the committed project Claude dot M D and dot Claude settings.json, not in a user file.

1.title: Features
1.text: Features. Session management. Sessions are saved: continue the latest (dash dash continue), resume one by I D or name (dash dash resume less than name greater than, name with dash n), fork to try another path (dash dash fork session); slash clear starts fresh; slash compact frees context. Slash commands. Built-in (slash init, slash memory, slash compact, or model, or permissions and more) and custom ones from markdown files. Headless mode. claude dash p "prompt" runs non-interactively and exits: for scripts and C I; add dash dash output format json (and dash dash json schema) for structured output. Streaming mode. dash dash output format stream-json emits newline-delimited Jason (Java Script Object Notation) events as they happen, for programs that show progress.

1.title: Features, continued
1.text: Features, continued. Permission modes. default (ask), accept Edits, plan (read-only exploration), auto (a classifier reviews actions and allows or blocks them), dont Ask, bypass Permissions (isolated environments only).

1.title: Features, continued
1.text: Features, continued. The figure shows this: Run modes: interactive, headless (dash p), streaming (stream-json) and automation with permission modes. Auto mode reduces prompts for autonomous runs while a classifier still reviews risky actions; bypass Permissions removes checks and belongs only in isolated environments. In C I use dash p, give context through Claude dot M D, pre-approve needed tools with dash dash allowed Tools, and prefer limits such as dash dash max turns.

1.title: Features, continued
1.text: Features, continued. Flags and modes evolve (for example dash dash bare skips auto-discovery of Claude dot M D, hooks and M C P (Model Context Protocol) servers for scripted runs). As of eight November two thousand twenty-six. Exam tip: Shared project standards go in the committed project Claude dot M D and dot Claude settings.json; a script or C I job uses claude dash p; a progress U I uses stream-json. Exam tip: Headless (dash p) is for scripts and C I; streaming Jason is for programs that show progress.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Components: Claude dot M D, rules, skills, commands (now skills), agents (subagents), agent memory, settings.json. Claude dot M D: User (personal), project (shared), directory; combined; slash init creates; slash memory inspects. Sessions: dash dash continue, dash dash resume less than name greater than, dash n to name, dash dash fork session, slash clear, slash compact. Headless: claude dash p; dash dash output format json; dash dash json schema. Streaming: dash dash output format stream-json. Permission modes: default, accept Edits, plan, auto (classifier), dont Ask, bypass Permissions (isolated only). Init checklist: slash init, commit Claude dot M D and settings, add rules, skills, commands.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A new teammate does not get the team's coding standards in Claude Code. Where were the standards most likely placed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. User-level files are personal; project-level files travel with the repository.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. What does slash init do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. slash init drafts the project instructions for you to review and commit.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A pipeline must run Claude Code without waiting for input. Which option fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. The dash p flag runs Claude Code non-interactively, prints the result and exits, which is what scripts need.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A program wants real-time progress events from a Claude Code run. Which output format fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. Streaming Jason emits newline-delimited events as they happen, so a program can show progress.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Select two. Which two statements about Claude Code components are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and B. Subagents and committed project instructions are core components; bypass mode is for isolated environments.

1.title: Answers at a Glance
1.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: B. Question two: A. Question three: C. Question four: D. Question five: A and B. In the next module, we continue the course.
